classification.difficultyReason: Draw explicitly named lines through supplied points and recognise their shared intersection as concurrency; no construction strategy must be devised.

content.prompt: Trace the six-point diagram to the right carefully into your exercise book.

spec.description: Six labelled points, with no connecting lines. A is above the base B–X–C; Z lies on AB and Y on AC. Ordinary source red markers are rendered black under house style. Coordinates reconstruct the intended midpoint arrangement rather than treating raster imprecision as mathematical data.
spec.mathematics: B, X, C are collinear; C, Y, A are collinear; A, Z, B are collinear. The three requested joining lines AX, BY and CZ are concurrent.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the six supplied points and labels are visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use your ruler to construct lines showing that:

answer.worked: Draw a straight line through $B$, $X$ and $C$, extending it beyond $B$ and $C$. All three points lie on this line.
Draw a straight line through $C$, $Y$ and $A$, extending it beyond $C$ and $A$. All three points lie on this line.
Draw a straight line through $A$, $Z$ and $B$, extending it beyond $A$ and $B$. All three points lie on this line.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Draw the lines $AX$, $BY$ and $CZ$. What can you say about these three lines?

answer.worked: Draw and extend $AX$, $BY$ and $CZ$ with a ruler. They all pass through one point, so they are concurrent.

spec.description: One shared completed figure showing the three collinear triples and the three concurrent joining lines. All lines extend beyond their defining points.
spec.mathematics: AX, BY and CZ meet at (7/3,1) in the chosen coordinate frame.
